newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: EUROMINISTER QUITS LOAN PANEL JOB IN PROTEST.
newsitem.headline: EUROMINISTER QUITS LOAN PANEL JOB IN PROTEST.

text.p: European Affairs Minister Laima Andrikiene has resigned as chairman of the foreign loans commission in protest at the inefficient use of such credits, the ministry said on Friday.
Andrikiene presented on Thursday her statement to Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius, the ministry said.

"Growing foreign loans, their inefficient use and the fact they are not used as intended...show that it is necessary to review the general borrowing principle and loan granting criteria," the ministry said in a statement.

"Without the support of the government in solving this problem, the minister refuses to head the commission and to take decisions on issuing state guarantees, relying on criteria and principles formed by the former government," it added.
Lithuania's foreign debt in hard currency was $1.267 million at the end of June versus $1.175 million at the start of the year. It was 13.8 percent of GDP.
Some $935 million of total foreign debt was taken in the name of state and $332 million with government guarantees.
